title: Equality at a stalk spreads for morphisms with finite locally free source
statement: Let $W$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $M,N$ sheaves of $\mathcal O_W$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $M$ finite locally free [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], and $x\in U\subseteq W$ with $U$ open. Let $f,g:M|_U\to N|_U$. Suppose for every open $V\subseteq U$ containing $x$ and every section $m$ of $M|_U$ on $V$, the germs [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] of $f(m)$ and $g(m)$ in $N_x$ agree. Then there is an open $Z\subseteq U$ containing $x$ on which the restrictions of $f$ and $g$ are equal. No finiteness condition is imposed on $N$.

source.place: Lemma 10.79.2, label lemma-map-between-finitely-presented; finite generator and finite relation argument specialized to a free frame

proof.text: The restriction-stalk comparison and representatives of arbitrary germs turn the assumed equality on local sections into equality of the two stalk maps on U. Restriction of M is finite locally free, by its comparison with pullback.

Choose a finite free frame near x in U. Apply equality of stalk maps to its finitely many basis germs. Use the existing finite-free germ-equality shrinking helper in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeStalkMapEquality (import all makes its private declarations available) to shrink until the two free-source maps agree.

Cancel the frame isomorphism. Map the resulting open back into W and use restriction composition and image-open isomorphisms to get the asserted restricted equality. Reuse restrict_map_injective_of_isIso from FiniteFreeStalkMapEquality to descend the equality along the image-open isomorphism. For rank zero the finite intersection has no extra conditions. Transport equality across natural isomorphisms with the existing private map_eq_of_iso from the same module, applied to the inverse natural isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Finite free sheaf argument proved in Lean by T3; repair reuses the private finite-germ and restriction-injectivity helpers of FiniteFreeStalkMapEquality through a proof-only import all. Second reading also reuses map_eq_of_iso instead of duplicating its naturality argument.

theorem exists_shrink_restrict_hom_eq_of_germs
    {W : Scheme.{u}} (M N : W.Modules) [M.IsFiniteLocallyFree]
    (x : W) (U : W.Opens) (hxU : x ∈ U)
    (f g : (restrictFunctor U.ι).obj M ⟶ (restrictFunctor U.ι).obj N)
    (h : ∀ (V : U.toScheme.Opens) (hxV : (⟨x, hxU⟩ : U.toScheme) ∈ V)
      (m : Γ((restrictFunctor U.ι).obj M, V)),
      N.presheaf.germ (U.ι ''ᵁ V) x ⟨⟨x, hxU⟩, hxV, rfl⟩ (Hom.app f V m) =
        N.presheaf.germ (U.ι ''ᵁ V) x ⟨⟨x, hxU⟩, hxV, rfl⟩ (Hom.app g V m)) :
    ∃ (V : W.Opens) (_ : x ∈ V) (hVU : V ≤ U),
      (restrictFunctor (W.homOfLE hVU)).map f =
        (restrictFunctor (W.homOfLE hVU)).map g
